defects.title: The default of exact is applied only when str is also missing
defects.trigger: rBioNet_search(table, column, str) with three inputs
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-15) rBioNet_search({'a', 'Urea'}, 2, 'Urea') stops at line 45 with 'Not enough input arguments.' (the default is set only for nargin < 3)
defects.expected: exact = 0 (partial match) when only exact is omitted

notes: Not a quarantine defect: USAGE/INPUTS list exact as required and all toolbox callers (ReconstructionCreator, ReconstructionTool, load_reaction) pass four inputs; recorded as limitation. Line 25 is covered by rBioNet_search(cell(0, 3), 2) (empty table, nothing compared). testRBioNetSaveLoad calls rBioNet_search once but tests rBioNetSaveLoad (two functions), so it is not a legacy test of this function only. The 'rxn'/'met' branch calls rBioNetSaveLoad('load', table) (already tested); the test writes the databases and rBioNetSettingsDB.mat in a tempname folder made the current folder (found before the tutorials' settings file). Other tables open a real msgbox that the test reads and closes (closeMessageBoxes pattern of testRBioNetSaveLoad).

No browser and no network: a stand-in web.m written into a tempname folder made the current folder records its arguments in a file (the test asserts which('web') is the stand-in, then clear('web') and removes the folder). The two message boxes (empty ID, unknown source) are real msgboxes, read and closed by the test. The KEGG address format (genome.jp/kegg-bin/show_pathway?ec01100+...) is pinned as written; whether the site still accepts it was not checked (internet).

testLoadReaction calls formula2mets once but tests loadReaction/balancecheck too, so it is not a legacy test of this function only. The regexprep '\[.+\]' is greedy (a name with two bracket groups would lose both); not probed, not recorded.

No browser: a tempname folder made the current folder holds stand-ins sammi.m (so which('sammi') names that folder and openSammi lists/opens files there instead of src/visualization/SAMMIM, which has no html files) and web.m (records its arguments), plus model.html, other.html and notes.txt. The listing of the no-input call is read with diary (no evalc); a caller's active diary is restored. The missing-file warning is checked with lastwarn (it still prints). Placed in testSAMMIM (testSammi also exists for this src folder).

defects.title: The second output is not assigned when no listed link has a non-zero width
defects.trigger: same structure with re1.width = {'0'}, [ref, list] = addColour(parsed, {'re1'})
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-15) 'Output argument "listRxnColour" (and possibly others) not assigned a value in the execution with "addColour" function.'

notes: Reproduction: ref = struct(); ref.re1.name = {'re1','HEX1'}; ref.re1.width = {'2.0'}; ref.re1.color = {'ff000000','ff000000'}; ref.re2.name = {'re2','PGI'}; ref.re2.width = {5}; ref.re2.color = {'ff000000'}; ref.r_info.ID = {'re1','re1','HEX1'; 're2','re2','PGI'}; [r2, l2] = addColour(ref, {'PGI'})  % error, re2 not coloured; [r1, l1] = addColour(ref, {'HEX1'})  % works; [r3, l3] = addColour(ref, {'re1', '#123456'})  % r3.re1.color = {'ffdef595','ffdef595'}. Also seen, not probed: line 122 tests isempty(strfind(name,'(e)')) before replacing '(e)', so the replacement never happens. No callers in the ledger, so no cascade.
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproductions: an ID in the last row of r_info.ID is never mapped; the html colour column is unused; the second output can be unassigned)

defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-15) prints 'p_st = 19 28', then 'Colon operands must be real scalars.' at line 25 (p_st keeps every strfind match)

defects.title: Debug output of the start index, the rest of the line and the end index

notes: Reproduction: [s, a, b] = position({'<reaction metaid="re1" id="re2">'}, 'id')  % error 'Colon operands must be real scalars.' (R2025a; older releases used the first element and would return 're1'). position({'<celldesigner:line width="1.0" color="ff000000"/>'}, 'color') works ('ff000000', 39, 46). Cascade for the lead: callers writeCD, writeXML and repairXML (and through writeCD colourAll, colourNode, colourNodeWhite) always call position(reText, 'width'/'color') on the '<celldesigner:line width=... color=...>' lines that parseCD recorded, where each name occurs once; the error needs the name twice in the line (data-dependent, not visible in the calling code).
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproduction: str_ID occurring twice in the line, e.g. 'id' inside 'metaid', gives a colon-operand error)
